# Inline AI

`Alt+I` asks the AI to change the thing you are in, in place, without going through the chat. This says what
must hold for it; `services/ui/README.md` says what is built.

## Inline is a category, not a second AI

The app has one AI agent (`ds.ai.agent`, `smash-agent`), one history (`Session.ai_history`) and one way to ask
(`Session.ask`). An inline turn is a chat turn asked from a place in the app instead of the chat box: think
of a slash command in the chat box that makes the answer come back in a set form. "Inline" survives only as:

| What | Why it can't go |
| --- | --- |
| **The answer's form** (`Inline.output_type`), with the rules, reference and check for writing it | it depends on the place: Python for a cell, SQL for the SmashDb box, one command for the Terminal, and for a widget the tool's own inputs (built from its schema, never per widget) |
| **A label** (`inline-edit`, `inline-fill`, `inline-terminal`, `inline-assign`) | categorical: the debug log's record, the Spend tab's split, the Agents tab's card, the quiet row in the chat |

Everything else is the chat's. There is no second agent with its own instructions, model or memory, no
separate runner, and no summary written into the history in place of the turn. A new inline place is an
`Inline(...)` passed to `Session.ask` (and a row in `inline.LABELS`), never a new `Agent(...)`.
Decided 2026-11-22.

## A widget is a function

A widget that has a tool (`Widget.tool` in `ui/widgets.py`) is a function: inputs in, a result
out. Everything that acts on a widget's inputs goes through that one contract, never through code written
for one widget:

| Part of the contract | Where |
| --- | --- |
| the inputs and their types | the tool's parameter schema, the one the chat agent gets (`ToolForm.schema`) |
| what counts as valid | the tool's own validator (`ToolForm.check`) |
| the inputs that made what is shown | the session's record of the call (`Session.calls`) |
| running it | the tool function; the result replaces the value where it is shown (`Session.put`) |

The tool form, the chat agent and the inline AI are three users of it. A new widget with a tool gets all
three by its row in `WIDGETS`.

## Rules

- **The AI proposes, the user runs.** In a widget the inline AI only fills the inputs. It never runs the tool:
  a run can cost outside requests (start.gg's rate budget) and replaces what is on screen.
- **A proposal is reviewable and reversible.** What the AI changed is marked, the old value is one hover
  away, and one key (Esc) puts the inputs back. As in an editor, where a proposal is a diff to accept.
- **A proposal is valid before it is shown.** It passes the tool's own validator; one that doesn't goes back
  to the model, and if it still doesn't, nothing in the form changes.
- **The AI works on what is on screen**: the inputs as typed, run or not, and its own last proposal.
- **And on the variables the instruction mentions** (`@q1`, experimental: `variables.md`, "Mentions"): it is
  told what they hold, as text. It still has no tools, so a big one is a summary.
- **In the Terminal it writes the command and never runs it**: the command is typed at the prompt, from the
  ask and the text on screen; Enter is the user's.
- **One key.** `Alt+I` means "inline AI here" everywhere: code in an editor, inputs in a widget, a command
  in the Terminal. An editor
  inside a widget (the SmashDb console's SQL box) keeps the editor meaning.
- **Proposed code comes formatted.** Python is run through `ruff format` at 88 columns after the model
  answers (`ui/format.py`; what ruff can't format, eg part of a statement, is shown as written). SQL has no
  formatter: the model is told the layout (UPPERCASE keywords, a clause per line; `SQL_FORMAT` in
  `ui/inline_edit.py`), so it is a request and not a guarantee.
- **Its real messages join the chat's history**, as a chat turn's do: the message (where it was asked, what
  the place shows, the instruction) and the answer as the model gave it. So the chat can be asked about an
  inline turn, and the next inline turn knows the last. A failed turn adds nothing. (Until 2026-11-22 the
  rule was "adds nothing to it".)
- **Bulky reference is sent, not kept.** What the answer needs but the conversation doesn't (table schemas
  and first rows, the session's variables, the Terminal's screen) goes as instructions for that turn
  (`Inline.context`), which are not part of the history: it is not sent again with every later turn. The
  message itself stays small.
- **The chat pane shows it as a quiet row** (kind `inline`): its label, where it was asked and the
  instruction on one dim line, quieter than a tool call; the answer folds open. "/assign" keeps its own row.
- **Nothing records what became of a proposal**: accepting or dropping one happens in the browser, and the
  backend isn't told. The history holds what was proposed.
- **Each turn is logged and costed like any chat turn**, under its label: the debug log's record, the Spend
  tab's split by agent, the title bar's context meter (it is part of the chat's size).
- **No tools.** The inline AI answers in one request from what it is given. Looking things up is the chat's
  job. The agent's tools are hidden for the turn (`InlineMode`), the ones a capability loaded in the chat
  too. It is one flag of the turn, not a different agent.
- **The answer arrives whole**, not streamed word by word: it has a form to be checked against.

## Adding a widget: ask about inline chat

When creating a widget, or giving an existing one a tool, **ask the user whether it should have the inline
chat** before building it. Don't decide silently either way.

- A widget with parameters (a `tool`) gets the inline chat by default, so say so and confirm: "this widget
  has inputs, so `Alt+I` will fill them. Is that what you want?"
- A widget without parameters gets none. Still ask: the user may want it to become function-like (give it
  a tool), or want the inline AI to do something else there (see "Not done yet").
- If the answer is no for a widget that has a tool, that is a new attribute on `Widget` (eg `inline_chat`)
  read where the AI button is drawn (`render.ai_toggle`), not a special case in the component.

## Not done yet

- **Table results have no function behind them.** A result finds its tool by its type
  (`widgets.form_for`), which only works while each tool returns its own type. Head to head, tournaments,
  event entrants and move frame data all return a table and are bound as plain DataFrames, so they get no
  form and no inline AI. The next step is for the call record (`Session.calls`) to say which tool made a
  value, and for the form to be found from that.
- **View controls are not inputs.** A table's row filter, sort and `SQL ▸`, the usage view's window and the
  videos page live in the view's own state (`render.Ui`), outside the contract above. Letting the inline AI
  drive them needs a second contract, "view parameters", per widget.
